title: A 150-Foot Deep-Sea Creature Is Longer Than a Blue Whale

scenes.text: Scientists filmed a deep-sea creature 150 feet long.
That's longer than a blue whale, the biggest animal alive.
It's a siphonophore, seen off Western Australia, drifting in the dark.
It isn't one body. It's a colony of tiny clones linked into a single long string.
The robot spotted it about 2,000 feet down, and it may be the longest animal ever recorded.
A single string of life longer than a whale.

description:
During a 2020 expedition off Western Australia, the Schmidt Ocean Institute filmed a siphonophore estimated at 150 feet, possibly the longest animal ever recorded.
It is a floating colony of tiny clones that work together as one animal.
What else do you think is hiding in the deep ocean?
first_comment: Bonus: the same expedition found up to 30 new species. What would you name this one?
